first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding currently has the strongest fit because onboarding completion is down and prior evidence indicates it can also improve activation and time-to-value. I would verify both onboarding records for durability and segment fit, while checking promotional-pricing evidence as the main alternative given competitor pressure. Sustainable qualified-revenue impact remains uncertain because the summarized onboarding evidence emphasizes early adoption, while pricing may introduce margin or retention risks not visible in the consolidated memory.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The confirmed shortened-flow test improved completion by 13%, time-to-value by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current declines. SMB signup simplification also lifted activation by 9% and qualified revenue by 4%, though its 1% retention decline warrants retention and qualified-revenue guardrails. Promotional pricing is rejected despite its short-term revenue lift because retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
